newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African benchmark bonds traipsed firmer in light volume Monday dealings on local institutional and suspected foreign interest with the market seen consolidating current levels over the next few days.
At 1420 GMT government's R150 stock yielded 14.10 percent, a level it had toyed with throughout the day, from 14.11 percent late on Friday.
"The market was traded lightly, nothing dramatic and I would say we're consolidating, something that started around Thursday last week," commented a senior debt trader.
Bullish sentiment over the next one to two months was being toned down due to concern over the delay in an official interest rate cut.
"There is general concern over the Bank rate and short rates which is putting a dampener on bullish sentiment."
Tuesday's range was seen similar to Monday with yields expected to stick around 14.10 percent.
No economic data is scheduled on the homefront but next week sees a barrage of indicators including crucial credit and money supply figures.
Foreigners bought 229.66 million rands worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 459.63 million rands worth on Thursday, the Bond Exchange said.
Bond Exchange turnover totalled 6.24 billion rand on Friday from 46.91 billion on Thursday -- a settlement day.
In currency dealings, the rand ended a sluggish session slightly up on the dollar after a good supply of export dollars in the market.
In addition, the local unit was unfazed by a recuperating dollar during the day.
The dollar/mark recovered to near 1.8250, buoyed by a solid Wall Street opening and fading fears of German central bank repo rate moves on Tuesday.
At 1420 GMT the currency was priced at 4.6815/6845 against the greenback from 4.6870/6900 at 1400 GMT on Friday.
"There was not too much in the way of dollar buying and I expect 4.66 to 4.70/71 to hold over the next few days," said a forex trader at a major local bank.
She said the week's direction would be dictated by U.S. dollar antics.
"It's difficult to see what the dollar is going to do next but that's where the focus will be."
The rand put in a mixed performance against the crosses, last priced at 0.3891/3895 on the German mark from 0.3882/3886 late Friday.
Rand/yen was at 25.1318/1586 from 25.9419/9792 and against sterling, it was last trading at 7.5396/5491 from 7.5441/5513.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.40 to 15.50 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 14.90 to 14.95 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage eased slightly to 8.555 billion rand on Saturday after falling to 8.563 billion rand on Friday.
